findings.title: Authorization check uses AND for team admin and owner, and allows any attendee
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner`. That is too strict for admins who are not owners, and the name says "or". Separately, any attendee of the booking can add guests, and the organizer is never notified for approval. Since the new guest list is unbounded, attendees can inject arbitrary emails into the organizer's event and calendar, and the host's mailer sends them invitations. Restrict to the organizer and team admins (use OR), and drop the attendee permission or document it.

findings.title: Case-sensitive dedupe and blacklist comparison
findings.body: The blacklist is lowercased, but `guest` is compared as-is, so `Foo@x.com` bypasses the blacklist. The existing-attendee check is also case-sensitive, so the same address can be added twice with a different case. Normalize guests to lowercase before comparing and storing.

findings.title: Calendar update runs unguarded after the DB write, with the wrong credentials and user
findings.body: Attendees are persisted before `updateCalendarAttendees`. If the calendar update throws, the guests are already saved, the mutation fails, and no emails are sent; a retry then hits the "unique" error. The EventManager is also built from `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. When an attendee or team admin performs the action, the organizer's calendar credentials are not used, so the calendar event is not updated.

findings.title: New-guest detection by exact email match, and no honoring of disabled-email settings
findings.body: `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` receives the raw `guests` input, not the filtered `uniqueGuests`. Existing attendees whose addresses appear in the input (for example blacklisted ones that were filtered out) get the wrong email, and case differences cause the same problem. In addition, `sendAddGuestsEmails` ignores the event type's `disableStandardEmails` metadata that sibling functions respect.

findings.title: Email failure swallowed with no error detail
findings.body: The catch block logs a generic string and drops the error object, making email failures impossible to debug. Use the logger and include `err`.

findings.title: Error toast built from the raw code and a translated message
findings.body: The message is always a non-empty template string, so the `unable_to_add_guests` fallback is never used. The user sees text like "BAD_REQUEST: ...". Zod validation errors from the server would also be passed through `t()` as raw JSON.

findings.title: Add guests action shown for all bookings in the edit menu
findings.body: The action is shown regardless of event-type settings such as seated events or the user's role, and regardless of whether the user is allowed. For non-permitted users the call just fails with FORBIDDEN.

findings.title: Array index used as React key
findings.body: Using the index as the key while rows can be removed from the middle makes inputs keep stale state and focus when one is deleted.
